name: Whakamaru eruption
d: A supereruption in New Zealand's central North Island laid down the Whakamaru ignimbrites, together more than 1,000 km3 of deposits. (date contested)
src: Wikipedia 'Whakamaru Caldera' (Froggatt et al. 1986; Matthews et al. 2012); Brown et al. 1998 https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70244160

name: Golygin Ignimbrite (Pauzhetka caldera)
d: Kamchatka's largest eruption of the last million years collapsed the 27 × 18 km Pauzhetka caldera.
src: Bindeman et al. 2010, JVGR 189:57–80, doi:10.1016/j.jvolgeores.2009.10.009; Davydova et al. 2021 Goldschmidt abstract https://goldschmidtabstracts.info/2021/6231.pdf

name: Mamaku Ignimbrite eruption
d: The Mamaku ignimbrite eruption formed the caldera now holding Lake Rotorua. Within days, the paired Ohakuri eruption followed nearby.
src: Gravley et al. 2007, GSA Bulletin, doi:10.1130/b25924.1; Wikipedia 'Rotorua Caldera'

name: Los Humeros caldera eruption (Xáltipan Ignimbrite)
d: The largest known eruption of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt formed the ~18 km Los Humeros caldera in Puebla.
src: Carrasco-Núñez et al. 2018, G-cubed 19:132–149, doi:10.1002/2017GC007044

name: Kos Plateau Tuff eruption
d: The largest known eruption of the Aegean arc spread pyroclastic flows across Kos and nearby islands.
src: Smith et al. 1996 (single-crystal 40Ar/39Ar, 161.3±1.1 ka); Bachmann et al. 2007 https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70170335

name: Aso-3 eruption
d: Aso's third great caldera-forming eruption buried much of central Kyushu under ignimbrite.
src: Albert et al. 2019, Quat. Geochronol. 52:103–131, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2019.01.005 (Table 1)

name: Kutcharo Kc-Hb (Kp IV) eruption
d: A large caldera-forming eruption at Kutcharo, Japan's largest Quaternary caldera, spread the Haboro ash across eastern Hokkaido.
src: Albert et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2019.01.005 (Table 1)

name: Toya caldera-forming eruption
d: The eruption formed the Toya caldera in southwest Hokkaido. Its ash fell across northern Japan.
src: Takarada 2019, Proc. Int. Meeting on Eruptive History and Informatics 2019-1 https://staff.aist.go.jp/s-takarada/papers/EHAI19-1_takarada.pdf

name: Ata eruption (Ata pyroclastic flow)
d: A caldera-forming eruption at the mouth of Kagoshima Bay spread ignimbrite and a widespread ash layer across Japan.
src: Albert et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2019.01.005

name: Kikai-Tozurahara eruption
d: A large eruption from the mostly submarine Kikai caldera south of Kyushu spread the K-Tz ash across Japan and the Pacific.
src: Albert et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2019.01.005

name: Aso-4 eruption
d: Japan's largest known eruption formed today's Aso caldera. Pyroclastic flows crossed the sea to Yamaguchi, and its ash reached Hokkaido.
src: Albert et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2019.01.005; Takarada 2019 https://staff.aist.go.jp/s-takarada/papers/EHAI19-1_takarada.pdf

name: Los Chocoyos eruption
d: A supereruption from the Atitlán caldera spread ash from the Pacific to the Gulf of Mexico. Its sulfur signal appears in both Greenland and Antarctic ice. (date contested)
src: Innes et al. 2025, Commun. Earth Environ. 6:137, doi:10.1038/s43247-025-02095-6; Cisneros de León et al. 2021, JQS 36:169–179, doi:10.1002/jqs.3265

name: Youngest Toba eruption (Youngest Toba Tuff)
d: The largest eruption of the last 2 million years formed Lake Toba on Sumatra and blanketed South Asia in ash.
src: Storey, Roberts & Saidin 2012, PNAS 109:18684–18688; Kutterolf et al. 2023, JVGR, doi:10.1016/j.jvolgeores.2023.107879

name: Maninjau caldera eruption
d: Silicic pyroclastic flows from Maninjau in West Sumatra covered about 8,500 km2 and left the caldera now holding Lake Maninjau.
src: Alloway et al. 2004, EPSL 227:121ff, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2004.08.014; Wikipedia 'Lake Maninjau'

name: Rotoiti eruption (Rotoehu Ash)
d: The Rotoiti ignimbrite eruption from the Ōkataina centre spread the Rotoehu Ash, a key marker layer across the North Island. (date contested)
src: Flude & Storey 2016, Quat. Geochronol. 33:13–23, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2016.01.002

name: Shikotsu caldera-forming eruption (Spfa-1/Spfl)
d: One of Hokkaido's largest eruptions formed the caldera holding Lake Shikotsu, near today's Sapporo.
src: Albert et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2019.01.005 (Table 1, after Uesawa et al. 2016)

name: Kutcharo Kc-Sr (Kp I) eruption
d: The youngest caldera-forming eruption at Kutcharo produced the Shoro ash, largely in phreatomagmatic explosions.
src: Albert et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.quageo.2019.01.005 (Table 1)

name: Campanian Ignimbrite eruption
d: The largest eruption in Europe of the last 200,000 years spread ash from Italy to Russia, near the time when Neanderthals disappeared.
src: Giaccio et al. 2017, Sci. Rep. 7:45940, doi:10.1038/srep45940

name: Aira caldera eruption (Ito ignimbrite, AT tephra)
d: The eruption formed the Aira caldera in Kagoshima Bay. The Ito ignimbrite ('shirasu') covered southern Kyushu, and the AT ash reached Korea and northern Japan.
src: Smith et al. 2013, QSR 67:121–137, doi:10.1016/j.quascirev.2013.01.026; Takarada 2019

name: Oruanui eruption
d: The world's most recent supereruption formed the basin now holding Lake Taupō, during the Last Glacial Maximum.

name: Neapolitan Yellow Tuff eruption
d: The second great caldera collapse of Campi Flegrei, the largest known trachytic phreatoplinian eruption, buried the area of today's Naples in yellow tuff.

name: Laacher See eruption
d: A Pinatubo-sized Plinian eruption in Germany's Eifel spread ash across central Europe just before the Younger Dryas cold spell.
src: Reinig et al. 2021, Nature 595:66–69
